subject: physics
question_text: The states of rest and motion are relative. Explain.

verification.note: Unit 3 has NO Long Answer section in either source book. The Fastrack (pp.6-8) lists 4 Very Short Answer and 6 Short Answer questions; the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.4-5) has a Short Answer section ONLY and no VSAQ section at all. So this VSAQ is the Fastrack’s alone. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. This exact cell was asked in the AP March 2026 paper, Section A question 11, which is recorded in appearances[].

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Motion in a Straight Line · 2 marks

steps.label: What relative means
lines: Rest and motion are not properties of a body
by itself. They are stated with respect to a
Change the frame and the answer changes.
steps.why: There is no way to test whether a body is truly at rest, so every statement about rest or motion is a statement about a comparison with something else.
common_mistakes: Saying a body is "really" at rest. There is no frame that is at absolute rest.

recall.must_convey: That rest and motion are stated with respect to a frame of reference, not on their own.

steps.memory_tip: Rest and motion are always "with respect to" something. Never on their own.
steps.margin_note: The phrase "frame of reference" is what earns this mark.

steps.label: The example

lines.text: A person sitting in a moving bus

lines: is at rest with respect to the bus, and is in
motion with respect to a person standing on
the road. Both statements are correct.
steps.why: The same person is described two ways at the same instant, which is the clearest proof that neither description is a property of the person.
common_mistakes: Giving an example with only one observer, which cannot show the idea at all.

recall.must_convey: That a person in a moving bus is at rest with respect to the bus and in motion with respect to the road.
accept: at rest with respect to the bus
moving with respect to the road

steps.memory_tip: One body, two observers, two correct answers. That is the whole idea.
steps.margin_note: Name BOTH observers or the example proves nothing.

insider_note: Asked in AP March 2026. One example carries this answer — the same body at rest for one observer and moving for another.
